the slow turning of the spin axis itself.
Angular momentum
IωI\omegaIω, a vector along the spin axis.
Gyroscopic couple
C=IωωpC = I\omega\omega_pC=Iωωp​, the couple needed to turn the spin axis; the frame feels an equal and opposite reaction couple.
Universal bearing
a joint that lets the arm swing freely in any direction about its end.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the inertia and spin
    I=mk2=8×0.152=0.18 kg m2,ω=2π×25060=26.18 rad/sI = mk^2 = 8 \times 0.15^2 = 0.18\ \text{kg m}^2,\qquad \omega = \frac{2\pi \times 250}{60} = 26.18\ \text{rad/s}I=mk2=8×0.152=0.18 kg m2,ω=602π×250​=26.18 rad/s
  2. Step 2Find the couple from the weight

    The weight at the end of the arm tries to tip it down.

    C=mgl=8×9.81×0.2=15.70 N mC = mgl = 8 \times 9.81 \times 0.2 = 15.70\ \text{N m}C=mgl=8×9.81×0.2=15.70 N m
  3. Step 3Find the precession speed

    Instead of falling, the arm precesses so that C=IωωpC = I\omega\omega_pC=Iωωp​.

    ωp=CIω=15.700.18×26.18=3.33 rad/s (about 32 rpm)\omega_p = \frac{C}{I\omega} = \frac{15.70}{0.18 \times 26.18} = 3.33\ \text{rad/s}\ (\text{about } 32\ \text{rpm})ωp​=IωC​=0.18×26.1815.70​=3.33 rad/s (about 32 rpm)

Answer The arm swings round horizontally at 3.33 rad/s about the vertical bearing axis.

Rattan's working uses 240 rpm and gets 3.47 rad/s. This is the spinning top and the bicycle wheel held by one end of its axle.

Problem 7.5 Gyroscopic couple on a turning aircraft

An aeroplane flying at 240 km/h turns left through a quarter circle of 60 m radius. The engine and propeller have a mass of 450 kg and radius of gyration 320 mm, and turn at 2000 rpm clockwise seen from the rear. Find the gyroscopic couple and its effect.

Rattan (2009), Example 17.3

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Speedvvv240 km/h
Turn radiusRRR60 m
Rotor massmmm450 kg
Radius of gyrationkkk0.32 m
SpinNNN2000 rpm, clockwise from the rear

Find

  • Gyroscopic couple and its effect

Terms used in this problem

Spin ω\omegaω
the fast rotation of the rotor about its own axis.
Precession ωp\omega_pωp​
the slow turning of the spin axis itself.
Angular momentum
IωI\omegaIω, a vector along the spin axis.
Gyroscopic couple
C=IωωpC = I\omega\omega_pC=Iωωp​, the couple needed to turn the spin axis; the frame feels an equal and opposite reaction couple.
Precession in a turn
the spin axis turns with the aircraft, at ωp=v/R\omega_p = v/Rωp​=v/R.
Effect
which way the reaction couple tips the aircraft: nose up or nose down.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the inertia and spin
    I=450×0.322=46.08 kg m2,ω=2π×200060=209.4 rad/sI = 450 \times 0.32^2 = 46.08\ \text{kg m}^2,\qquad \omega = \frac{2\pi \times 2000}{60} = 209.4\ \text{rad/s}I=450×0.322=46.08 kg m2,ω=602π×2000​=209.4 rad/s
  2. Step 2Find the precession speed
    v=2403.6=66.67 m/s,ωp=66.6760=1.111 rad/sv = \frac{240}{3.6} = 66.67\ \text{m/s},\qquad \omega_p = \frac{66.67}{60} = 1.111\ \text{rad/s}v=3.6240​=66.67 m/s,ωp​=6066.67​=1.111 rad/s
  3. Step 3Find the couple
    C=Iωωp=46.08×209.4×1.111=10 720 N mC = I\omega\omega_p = 46.08 \times 209.4 \times 1.111 = 10\,720\ \text{N m}C=Iωωp​=46.08×209.4×1.111=10720 N m
  4. Step 4Find the effect

    For this spin direction a left turn gives a reaction couple that raises the nose and lowers the tail.

Answer About 10.7 kN m, raising the nose and lowering the tail.

A right turn would lower the nose.

Problem 7.6 Gyroscopic effects on a ship

A ship's turbine rotor of 2.2 t and radius of gyration 320 mm turns at 1800 rpm clockwise seen from aft. Find the gyroscopic couple and its effect when (i) the ship turns right on a 250 m radius at 25 km/h, (ii) it pitches with the bow rising at 0.8 rad/s, (iii) it rolls at 0.1 rad/s.

Rattan (2009), Example 17.4

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Rotor massmmm2200 kg
Radius of gyrationkkk0.32 m
SpinNNN1800 rpm
Turn250 m radius at 25 km/h
Pitching rate0.8 rad/s
Rolling rate0.1 rad/s

Find

  • Couple and effect in each case

Terms used in this problem

Spin ω\omegaω
the fast rotation of the rotor about its own axis.
Precession ωp\omega_pωp​
the slow turning of the spin axis itself.
Angular momentum
IωI\omegaIω, a vector along the spin axis.
Gyroscopic couple
C=IωωpC = I\omega\omega_pC=Iωωp​, the couple needed to turn the spin axis; the frame feels an equal and opposite reaction couple.
Bow, stern, aft
front of the ship, back of the ship, towards the back.
Steering, pitching, rolling
turning in the horizontal plane; bow rising and falling; tilting side to side about the fore-and-aft axis.
Starboard, port
the right and left sides looking forward.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the inertia and spin
    I=2200×0.322=225.3 kg m2,ω=2π×180060=188.5 rad/sI = 2200 \times 0.32^2 = 225.3\ \text{kg m}^2,\qquad \omega = \frac{2\pi \times 1800}{60} = 188.5\ \text{rad/s}I=2200×0.322=225.3 kg m2,ω=602π×1800​=188.5 rad/s
  2. Step 2Case (i): steering
    ωp=25/3.6250=0.0278 rad/s,C=225.3×188.5×0.0278=1180 N m\omega_p = \frac{25/3.6}{250} = 0.0278\ \text{rad/s},\qquad C = 225.3 \times 188.5 \times 0.0278 = 1180\ \text{N m}ωp​=25025/3.6​=0.0278 rad/s,C=225.3×188.5×0.0278=1180 N m
  3. Step 3Case (ii): pitching
    C=225.3×188.5×0.8=33 980 N mC = 225.3 \times 188.5 \times 0.8 = 33\,980\ \text{N m}C=225.3×188.5×0.8=33980 N m
  4. Step 4Case (iii): rolling

    Rolling is about the fore-and-aft axis, parallel to the spin axis, so the spin axis does not turn.

    C=0C = 0C=0
  5. Step 5State the effects

    (i) lowers the bow and raises the stern; (ii) turns the ship to starboard.

Answer 1.18 kN m (bow down); 34.0 kN m (turns to starboard); no couple when rolling.

Problem 7.7 Limiting speed of a car on a bend

A 2200 kg rear-engined car has wheels with Iw=2.4I_w = 2.4Iw​=2.4 kg m² each and diameter 660 mm. The engine parts have Ie=1.2I_e = 1.2Ie​=1.2 kg m², with gear ratio 3, turning the same way as the wheels. The centre of mass is 550 mm high and the track is 1.5 m. Find the limiting speed on an 80 m bend.

Rattan (2009), Example 17.6

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Car massmmm2200 kg
Each wheelIwI_wIw​2.4 kg m²
Wheel radiusrwr_wrw​0.33 m
EngineIeI_eIe​1.2 kg m²
Gear ratioGGG3
Height of GGGhhh0.55 m
Trackwww1.5 m
Bend radiusRRR80 m

Find

  • Speed at which the inner wheels lift

Terms used in this problem

Spin ω\omegaω
the fast rotation of the rotor about its own axis.
Precession ωp\omega_pωp​
the slow turning of the spin axis itself.
Angular momentum
IωI\omegaIω, a vector along the spin axis.
Gyroscopic couple
C=IωωpC = I\omega\omega_pC=Iωωp​, the couple needed to turn the spin axis; the frame feels an equal and opposite reaction couple.
Track www
distance between the left and right wheels.
Centrifugal couple
the outward force mv2/Rmv^2/Rmv2/R acting at height hhh, tending to overturn the car.
Wheel reaction
the upward force of the road on each wheel. The car tips over when the inner reactions fall to zero.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the static load per wheel
    mg4=2200×9.814=5396 N\frac{mg}{4} = \frac{2200 \times 9.81}{4} = 5396\ \text{N}4mg​=42200×9.81​=5396 N
  2. Step 2Find the gyroscopic couple

    Spin v/rwv/r_wv/rw​ (engine GGG times faster), precession v/Rv/Rv/R.

    Cg=(4Iw+GIe)rwR v2=9.6+3.60.33×80 v2=0.5 v2C_g = \frac{(4I_w + G I_e)}{r_w R}\,v^2 = \frac{9.6 + 3.6}{0.33 \times 80}\,v^2 = 0.5\,v^2Cg​=rw​R(4Iw​+GIe​)​v2=0.33×809.6+3.6​v2=0.5v2
    per wheel: ±Cg2w=±0.167 v2\text{per wheel: } \pm\frac{C_g}{2w} = \pm 0.167\,v^2per wheel: ±2wCg​​=±0.167v2
  3. Step 3Find the centrifugal couple
    Cc=mv2Rh=2200×0.5580 v2=15.13 v2,per wheel ±5.04 v2C_c = \frac{m v^2}{R}h = \frac{2200 \times 0.55}{80}\,v^2 = 15.13\,v^2,\qquad \text{per wheel } \pm 5.04\,v^2Cc​=Rmv2​h=802200×0.55​v2=15.13v2,per wheel ±5.04v2
  4. Step 4Set the inner-wheel reaction to zero

    Both couples take load off the inner wheels.

    5396=(0.167+5.04) v2,v2=10365396 = (0.167 + 5.04)\,v^2,\qquad v^2 = 10365396=(0.167+5.04)v2,v2=1036
    v=32.2 m/s=116 km/hv = 32.2\ \text{m/s} = 116\ \text{km/h}v=32.2 m/s=116 km/h

Answer 32.2 m/s, about 116 km/h.

The centrifugal couple dominates; the gyroscopic part is only about 3% of it here.

7.AFind the height of a Watt governor at 100 rpm.

  1. Step 1Use h=895/N2h = 895/N^2h=895/N2
    h=8951002=0.0895 mh = \frac{895}{100^2} = 0.0895\ \text{m}h=1002895​=0.0895 m

Answer 89.5 mm.

7.BA Porter governor (equal arms) has balls of 2 kg and a sleeve of 18 kg. Compared with a Watt governor at the same height, how much faster does it run?

  1. Step 1Take the speed ratio
    NPNW=m+Mm=10=3.16\frac{N_P}{N_W} = \sqrt{\frac{m + M}{m}} = \sqrt{10} = 3.16NW​NP​​=mm+M​​=10​=3.16

Answer About 3.16 times faster.

7.CA rotor with I=10I = 10I=10 kg m² spins at 300 rad/s and is precessed at 0.5 rad/s. Find the gyroscopic couple.

  1. Step 1Apply C=IωωpC = I\omega\omega_pC=Iωωp​
    C=10×300×0.5=1500 N mC = 10 \times 300 \times 0.5 = 1500\ \text{N m}C=10×300×0.5=1500 N m

Answer 1500 N m.
